title: Learner 01 | Day 145: Integration boundaries and modular monoliths
body:
## Goal

Integration boundaries and modular monoliths

## Implementation contract

**File:** `src/learnforge/specializations/learner_01/experience/baseline.py`

**Method/unit:** `run_baseline`

**Why here:** This is inside your owned AI/ML capability and the named layer. Model/data SDK details stay in adapters, rules in core, and commands/results in experience. It plugs into the same shared project architecture as other capabilities.

**Inputs and expected outputs:** The same workspace identity flows end to end; each module has an explicit dependency; failures are visible at the right step.

**Boundaries:** Keep the change inside the owned capability and preserve accepted behavior.

## Research hints

1. Research **Integration boundaries and modular monoliths**. Which rule explains your named unit’s behavior?
2. Search `site:docs.python.org Integration boundaries and modular monoliths`; use [Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3.13/tutorial/) for the relevant small section.
3. Predict one changed input/timing case, run it, and explain each changed value before applying the finding.

## Done

- [ ] Demonstrate this unit’s normal and boundary/failure cases in the working feature.
- [ ] Show the actual run and explain one changed case using concrete values.

**Question of the Day:** What belongs in a cache key for an access-controlled RAG answer?

**Review with @GlidingScorpion:** run the named unit; show actual output and each relevant line’s purpose, before/after values and project contribution.

[Exact task walkthrough and contracts](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/LearnForge/blob/main/lessons/learner-01/day-145.md) · [Shared daily lesson](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/LearnForge/blob/main/days/day-145.md)
architecture_topic: Prefer clear internal boundaries first, then use evidence to decide whether a network boundary is useful.
